newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: AWF cuts Australian 1997/98 barley forecast.
newsitem.headline: AWF cuts Australian 1997/98 barley forecast.

text.p: Private forecaster Australian Wheat Forecasters Pty Ltd (AWF) said on Friday it had reduced its forecast for Australia's 1997/98 (April/March) barley crop to 6.140 million tonnes from 6.445 million in June.

In South Australia, the key barley producing state, soil conditions have allowed sown crops to germinate in most areas, AWF said. "Crops have been receiving just enough rain to keep them going, but there is concern that a large number of crops may fail to mature," the forecaster said. AWF said some crops in northern agricultural areas of South Australia had not emerged.
"The situation applies in the South Australian Mallee as well," it said. "It is not too late to sow more barley, but given the dry soils this is not currently a practical option."
AWF said rainfall was well below average for the first 2-1/2 months of the current growing season.
AWF said growing conditions for barley had been excellent for Western Australia over the past month.
"The crop was sown earlier than last year with the potential for significantly longer growing season in the southern barley areas of Western Australia," it said.
AWF said frowers had the field conditions to seed more barley, however most growers were content to retain their earlier cropping programmes.
"Growers have applied more fertiliser to barley crop this year," the forecaster said.
"This should assist them to achieve better yields and given a soft finish to the growing season later in the year, a higher proportion of malting or manufacturing categories," it said.
In Victoria, the eastern Mallee crops were growing well, and this applied also to Wimmera, AWF said. However, it said there was less than normal stored soil moisture.

"Growers are aware that substantial rains are still required, and the rain patterns recently received have all been light," AWF said. "Many Mallee areas have not yet been sown. Seeding will proceed if a general rain is received by the first week of August."
The southern areas of New South Wales had very good prospects of high yields and malting quality, the forecaster said.
"Northern areas are growing on stored soil moisture and this could continue for another month," it said.
AWF said the Queensland barley crop needed rain in the near future and prospects have declined over the past month.
